h: More than just cars at the old dye works
p: The building itself is part of the story. The Backbarrow works once produced the famous Dolly Blue laundry whitener, and older visitors sometimes remember the little bags of it from wash days long ago. Mills and works lined the River Leven here because of the water power, and the museum's riverside setting is a nice reminder of that industrial past in what's now such a peaceful valley.

Inside, it's the variety that wins people over. Alongside the cars there are scooters, vintage bicycles, toy cars and pedal cars that might spark a few memories, plus all manner of motoring signs and garage bits. Kids enjoy hunting for things they recognise, while grown-ups end up saying "I had one of those" more times than they'd care to admit.

The museum has its own café overlooking the river, which is a lovely spot for a cuppa and a cake. Grab a table by the window if you can, as watching the water rush past is properly relaxing after a few hours on your feet.

A few practical tips: give yourself a good two to three hours if you like reading the displays, and a bit more if you're a Bluebird enthusiast. The site is easy to find just off the A590, and it works well as a rainy-day plan or as a stop on the way into or out of the Lakes.

For a gentle stroll afterwards, Newby Bridge and the southern end of Windermere are only a few minutes away. Holker Hall, where the collection started out, is also within reach if you fancy a stately home and gardens to round off the day.
